title: Specmetry check run result v1
description: Output of `specmetry check run --json`. With --json, stdout carries exactly one JSON document conforming to this schema and nothing else; the checks' own stdout and stderr are streamed to the caller's stderr. Without --json, check output is passed through to stdout/stderr unchanged. In both modes check output is never persisted. This document is written only when the batch completes: exit code 10 when any run is not pass, otherwise 0 (also for an empty batch). Exit code 6 with --isolation required when isolation cannot be established (no run is recorded). A batch that stops early (cancellation, a process tree not confirmed ended, an unreadable end context, incomplete output forwarding, a persistence failure) writes error.v1 instead, with exit code 6, or 1 for internal errors (priority 1 > 6 > 10 > 0). Exit code 6 does not mean a rerun is safe: earlier runs, and possibly the current one, may already be recorded.

is_target_snapshot.description: Batch summary only: true when every run's head_start equals the delivery target snapshot; with no runs, true when HEAD at the start of the command equals it; false when there is no target snapshot. It never decides whether a run counts: delivery status is derived from each run's own fields, so a qualifying run on the target snapshot counts even when this is false.

isolation.description: Requested isolation mode. The MVP supports off and required (required always fails with exit 6 until the isolated executor ships); auto is reserved for the isolated executor.

items.description: One recorded run. Its result, failure_kind and exit_code agree (WP2.5 D14): pass has no failure kind and exit code 0; fail is nonzero_exit with a nonzero exit code, or null for a Unix signal; error is timeout, spawn_error, input_missing, context_changed, or not_found (read only). timeout, spawn_error and input_missing have no exit code, and the last two a duration of 0; context_changed may carry any exit code, 0 included, and never qualifies. A qualifying run has a head_start and a clean start. An error run can qualify, and no exit code is bounded.

failure_kind.description: nonzero_exit carries the interpreter's final exit status; failures masked inside the command string are not detected. not_found is reserved: the observed runner never produces it, but readers must accept it. context_changed also covers an end context that could not be read and a process tree not confirmed ended; it does not prove that the context changed.

isolation_fallback_reason.description: Only with isolation auto: why isolation could not be established before the run, so it ran as observed in the caller's worktree. A change detected in the private snapshot after the run is not a fallback: that run is recorded as error/context_changed and is not qualifying.
